one_line: Seventeenth‑century Warkari poet-saint of Dehu whose abhangas shaped devotion to Vitthal across the Marathi-speaking world.

appearance.age_look: Looks like a wiry man in his late 30s to early 40s, lean from walking pilgrimages, with modest, unassuming posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, softly defined jaw, straight nose, faint smile lines around the mouth and eyes, thin moustache, calm reflective eyes with a gentle upward gaze, default expression serene and inwardly focused as if listening to a bhajan.
appearance.hair: Black hair kept short and neatly combed back, mostly hidden under a simple off-white cotton turban wrapped low and flat around the head, with one small folded tail of cloth tucked at the side.
appearance.costume: He wears a plain, long-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton kurta (traditional angarkha-style without ornate overlaps, tied inside, with a modest round neck), over a simple un-dyed cotton dhoti wrapped firmly to the ankles with neat pleats at the front; a narrow, soft, pale-saffron cotton shawl (uttariya) drapes from his left shoulder across the chest and over the right forearm, hinting at Warkari renunciation; his feet are in simple wooden paduka sandals with toe knobs, and he has minimal jewellery—only a thin tulsi-bead mala around his neck and a single small copper bangle on his right wrist.
appearance.signature: A tanpura-like ektara: a single-stringed wooden lute with a rounded gourd body in warm brown, a long pale-wood neck, and a simple cloth strap, which he carries gently in his left hand or rests against his shoulder, symbolizing his abhangas and kirtan singing.

ref_desc: Sant Tukaram is a lean, medium-brown man in his late 30s–40s with an oval face, thin moustache, short black hair under an off-white turban, wearing a plain off-white kurta, ankle-length dhoti, pale-saffron shawl and wooden paduka, carrying a brown single-string ektara.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Sant Tukaram as a historically grounded 17th-century Warkari poet: a lean man in his late 30s–40s with a warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, oval face, calm eyes with a gentle inward-looking gaze, and a thin moustache. His short black hair is almost entirely hidden under a simple off-white cotton turban wrapped low and flat around his head with a small folded tail at the side. He wears a modest, long-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton kurta with a round neck, plain and unadorned, over a neatly wrapped off-white cotton dhoti that reaches his ankles with clean front pleats. A narrow pale-saffron cotton shawl (uttariya) is draped from his left shoulder diagonally across his chest and over his right forearm, suggesting quiet renunciation. On his feet are simple wooden paduka sandals with toe knobs. His only ornaments are a thin tulsi-bead mala around his neck and a single small copper bangle on his right wrist. In his left hand or resting against his shoulder he carries a single-string ektara with a warm brown gourd body and pale wooden neck, his signature instrument for singing abhangas. Use a soft, earthy palette of off-white, pale saffron, warm brown, light beige and soft black, and present him from multiple angles to emphasize the consistent turban, kurta, dhoti, shawl, paduka sandals, and ektara, with dignified yet simple anime energy and fully modest clothing.
